question.worked_solution:
First, we find the roots of the characteristic polynomial:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda -5 & =0 \\ (\lambda +5)(\lambda -1) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =-5,1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general solution to the differential equation is

$$
y=A{e}^{-5x}+B{e}^{x}.
$$

Now we find the constants $A$ and $B$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(1)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
A{e}^{-5}+Be=1.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=7,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
{y}^{′}=-5A{e}^{-5x}+B{e}^{x}.
$$

Then, we substitute ${y}^{′}(1)=7$ into the above to get

$$
-5A{e}^{-5}+Be=7.
$$

Putting the two equations from above together, we have the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}A{e}^{-5}+Be=1 \\ -5A{e}^{-5}+Be=7\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $A=-{e}^{5},B=2{e}^{-1}.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-{e}^{5}\cdot {e}^{-5x}+2{e}^{-1}\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =-{e}^{-5x+5}+2{e}^{x-1}.\end{aligned}
$$
